title: Size and Usage of Endowment Funds of Autonomous Universities in Past Five Years
what_it_is: Size and Usage of Endowment Funds of Autonomous Universities in Past Five Years

sections.label: University endowment sizes 2017
sections.summary: End-2017 endowment sizes: NUS $5.9 billion, NTU $1.9 billion, SMU $1 billion, SUTD $1.1 billion, SIT and SUSS $0.4 billion each.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Based on these reports, the sizes at the end of financial year 2017 are: National University of Singapore (NUS), $5.9 billion; Nanyang Technological University (NTU), $1.9 billion; Singapore Management University, $1 billion; Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), $1.1 billion; Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), both $0.4 billion each.

sections.label: Endowment income for subsidised education
sections.summary: The biggest use of endowment income is paying operating expenditure for delivering subsidised education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The biggest use of endowment income is to pay for operating expenditure in delivering subsidised education.

sections.label: Comparing university endowment numbers
sections.summary: Numbers need breaking down to compare universities, and there is currently no limit as endowments were built over about 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We really need to break down the numbers to compare NUS, NTU, SUTD and so on and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There is currently not a limit because our universities have started building endowments maybe over the last 20 years or so.

sections.label: Encouraging donations with government matching
sections.summary: So long as there are good uses and donors give, the Government will continue matching one-to-one or 1.5-to-one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And so, they have good uses for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And so long as there are such good uses, and donors are prepared to part with their donations to support the institution, then we should encourage that and the Government will continue to match one-to-one or 1.5-to-one.

sections.label: Matching rates for new universities
sections.summary: New universities built up $400 million each, with Government matching three-to-one, while established universities with larger reserves get much less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Within a short period, they have built up $400 million each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And part of the reason is that, from the Government's point of view, for the new universities, we match three-to-one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, for every endowment fund dollar that you raise, we match three-to-one, whereas for the much more established universities with a larger reserve, we will match much less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Having said that, I do not think we want to be too draconian in redistributing the endowment.
